intro.title: Styled Component Pattern
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple, reusable button component using the Styled Component Pattern in Angular. You'll learn how to encapsulate styles directly within a TypeScript component to keep your UI elements modular and self-contained. The core concept involves using Angular's component decorator to define inline styles, avoiding external CSS files for small, focused components. You'll work with the @Component decorator, template literals for HTML, and TypeScript to create a styled button that can be easily reused across your application.
intro.usecase: The Styled Component Pattern is widely used in enterprise Angular applications where consistent, reusable UI components are essential. You'll see this pattern implemented in design systems for dashboard widgets, data tables with custom styling, and branded form controls that maintain visual consistency across an application. Developers use this approach when building complex interfaces like admin panels, e-commerce product cards, or notification systems where each component needs its own encapsulated styling logic. This pattern helps teams scale UI development while ensuring maintainability and theme consistency across large applications.
